doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Making a living only from music, then and now
summary: He never did other work after high school and was fortunate; younger musicians today must piece together theater, community theater, concerts and dance gigs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: What a way to make a living.

Well you know I never did anything — other kind of work after high school. I worked when I was in high school I did a little other work, but I never did anything else except music, I was able to make my living at it, I was fortunate. Because that doesn’t happen to very many people. And it’s probably harder now even than it was then. I know that some of my younger friends now really have to do a lot, I mean have to do everything. A little bit of theater and then maybe community theater, which is a lower scale, places like the © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
Schubert across the street which has a great scale. If you get one of those jobs that pays good money. And they have to do concerts with little orchestras or they do dance gigs and whatever they can.
